LLM auditresponse for grabbit.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided script `grabbit.sh` is a launcher script for an Electron-based application. It sets up environment variables such as `CHROME_DESKTOP` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, determines the correct application entry point based on the existence of specific files or directories (e.g., `app.asar`, `app`, or `app.asar.unpacked`), and conditionally disables the Electron sandbox when running as root (unless `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` is set). The use of `exec` to launch the application is standard practice for wrapper scripts and targets a locally installed Electron binary with a version placeholder (`@electronversion@`), which is typical in templated packaging.

No malicious patterns are present. The script does not use `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, `base64`, or other commands commonly associated with code injection or data exfiltration. All operations are confined to local file checks and environment setup. The conditional `--no-sandbox` flag is a known Electron packaging pattern, though it reduces security when running as root — this is a documented and expected trade-off in such contexts, not evidence of malice.

The script appears to be a standard runtime wrapper generated from a template (evident from `@appname@` and `@electronversion@` placeholders), which will be substituted during package build. There is no indication of injected backdoors, unauthorized network activity, or tampering with system files.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard build process for the `grabbit-git` package, a download manager based on aria2 and Electron. It fetches source code from the official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/ricode-labs/grabbit`), applies necessary patches for packaging, installs dependencies via `npm`, builds the application using `npm run package`, and installs the resulting files into the package directory. All operations are consistent with typical AUR packaging practices for Electron-based applications.

Several aspects of the script are security-relevant but not malicious. It uses `sha256sums=('SKIP')` for the Git source, which is expected and acceptable for VCS packages. The build process sets up a controlled environment using `nvm` to manage Node.js versions and configures Electron to use a system-installed binary via `ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1`, avoiding redundant downloads. It also modifies `forge.config.ts` to use a locally generated Electron zip, which is a legitimate technique to avoid re-downloading Electron during packaging.

No evidence of obfuscated code, unauthorized network requests, or data exfiltration was found. The `sed` commands patch internal paths to use system directories, and the `find ... sed` command hardens the code against unintended resource paths. The modifications to `src/main/tasks.ts` add a stub function, which is benign. All actions serve the purpose of integrating the upstream application securely into the Arch Linux system.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard AUR packaging; no malicious behavior detected</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD builds the Grabbit download manager from its declared upstream GitHub repository (github.com/ricode-labs/grabbit), using the system electron42 package, nvm-managed Node 24, npm, and system aria2c. The network surface is unremarkable: a standard VCS source (SKIP checksum is required for -git sources), the official npm registry, and nodejs.org through nvm. There are no curl|bash pipelines, no base64/hex obfuscation, no eval of fetched content, and no data exfiltration. File operations stay within srcdir/pkgdir; the only system path touched is /usr/lib/electron42, which is read and zipped locally so electron-forge reuses the system Electron instead of downloading one from the network.

The unusual steps — sed rewrites of process.resourcesPath in src/, insertion of electronZipDir, dir: true and asarUnpack into forge.config.ts, and a stub addUnfinishedTasks() function — are plain-text, visible build adaptations needed to package against system Electron rather than a bundled one. They serve the package's stated purpose and contain no hidden payloads. The companion launcher grabbit.sh is a declared source with a pinned sha256 (its content is not visible in this file, but it is part of the AUR repo and checksummed).

Hygiene notes only: the git source tracks a mutable default branch (normal for -git packages), and npm install runs dependency lifecycle scripts from the official npm registry — an inherent npm supply-chain surface, but standard AUR practice and not injected malice. Nothing in this file warrants an UNSAFE decision.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Safe: standard Electron AUR build; no injected malice, only hygiene notes.</summary>
